title: The Ellington sound on radio and working through the Depression
summary: You could tell it was Ellington within seconds on radio, and the band worked everywhere through the Depression while others starved.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Well, you take like in those days, I mean, in the radio time when there wasn't TV, you know, there were bands on the radio. Well, you could tell it was Duke's band the minute he got on the radio because it's a complete different style of arrangements and music, the way he had it all cut up and fixed up, that the minute it come on the air everybody knew it was Ellington. And all during the Depression we were working when the other bands were starving, because people wanted to hear that sound.
Did you work just the major cities during the Depression years?
People had money enough to come out and hear the band?
